forcing_mechanism.evidence: Employers with 150 to 249 staff must report pay gaps by 7 June 2027, and discrimination compensation has no cap (Art. 9(3), Art. 16(4)).

findable.evidence: France Travail job ads and SIRENE name French companies with NAF code and staff band, and no catalogue dataset covers Spanish employers by sector.

early.evidence: Live job ads and monthly SIRENE files are available now, 8 months before the 7 June 2027 reporting deadline for 150 to 249 staff.

gap_evidence.evidence: A France Travail ad with an empty salaire field is not proof, because employers can give pay before the interview or otherwise (Art. 5(1)).

crowding.evidence: Payroll and HR suites already hold the pay data that Art. 9 reporting uses, so every vendor in the category will pitch it.

list_recipes.filter: codeNAF 55, 56, 47 or 41-43; trancheEffectifEtab 10-249 staff; dateCreation after 7 June 2026
list_recipes.gap_evidence: live ads with an empty salaire field
list_recipes.metric: share of the company's live ads without a salary
list_recipes.caveat: Employers can give starting pay before the interview or by other means, so an ad without salary does not prove non-compliance (Art. 5(1)).

list_recipes.filter: activitePrincipale NAF 55, 56, 47 or 41-43; trancheEffectifs bands covering 150-249 staff
list_recipes.gap_evidence: none in the data; the staff band only shows the 7 June 2027 pay gap reporting duty applies
list_recipes.metric: months left until the 7 June 2027 reporting deadline
list_recipes.caveat: SIRENE shows which companies fall under the 2027 reporting duty, not which ones have prepared for it.
